PockPock Agent 0.2.3 brings connectors and cloud models to the Mac. It is the same app as 0.2.2, which came out for Windows only because GitHub's Mac build machines were unavailable, now built for Windows and both kinds of Mac.

## Download

| Your computer | Download |
|---|---|
| Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) | [PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-Setup.exe) |
| Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer) | [PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-arm64.dmg) |
| Mac with an Intel processor | [PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/releases/latest/download/PockPock-Agent-mac-x64.dmg) |

**Already using 0.2.1 or 0.2.2 on Windows?** PockPock updates itself: press **Restart to update** when it appears, or check in **Settings → Updates**. On a Mac, or from 0.1.0, download and install it once, the same way as the first time. Your chats, settings and models are kept.

**New to PockPock?** Open the downloaded file, then press **Set up PockPock**; setup installs everything else. Windows may show **"Windows protected your PC"** because PockPock is not code-signed yet: press **More info**, then **Run anyway**. On a Mac, see the [installation guide](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/wiki/Installation).

## What's new since 0.2.1

- **Connectors.** A new **Connectors** page connects **GitHub**, **Email** (Gmail, iCloud Mail, Yahoo Mail, Fastmail or your own mail servers), **Telegram**, **Slack**, **Discord** and **Notion**. You create a key in the app and paste it; PockPock checks it with the app before saving, and a refused key is not saved.
- **The agent can use them.** A connected app gives the **OpenClaw** engine tools for it: read issues and pull requests, search and read your mail, read the messages sent to your bot, read channels and pages. Sending an email, posting a message or opening an issue asks you first unless you chose Full access.
- **Your keys stay on your computer.** Connector and cloud keys are stored encrypted by Windows or the macOS Keychain and are never shown again. **Disconnect** deletes the key and takes the tools away.
- **Cloud models.** A new **Cloud models** page connects NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter or Alibaba Cloud Model Studio. You bring your own account and API key and pay the service directly; PockPock checks the key before saving it, and a refused key is not saved.
- **Cloud models in the model menus.** Once connected, the service's chat models appear in the model menus of **Chat**, **PockPock Agent**, **OpenClaw** and **NemoClaw**, listed under **Cloud models · sent to the provider**. Choose up to 40 models per service.
- **Your key stays on your computer.** **Replace key** stores a new key and keeps your chosen models; **Disconnect** deletes the key from the computer and removes the service's models from every menu.

## Good to know

- On Windows, 0.2.3 changes nothing from 0.2.2 except how the installers are built.
- The Mac versions are now built on an Intel Mac for both Apple silicon and Intel.
- Connectors work with the **OpenClaw** engine for now. Telegram, Slack and Discord act as a bot you create, not as your personal account. Outlook.com and Microsoft 365 mail cannot be connected, because Microsoft no longer accepts app passwords for mail.
- Connectors and cloud models are new and have had little testing with real accounts. Please [report problems](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/issues/new/choose).
- A cloud model receives the messages, attached files and tool results of the chats that use it, under your own account. It is used only when you choose it by name; Smart route and the agent's automatic model choice consider local models only.
- When a chosen cloud model fails (bad key, no credit, rate limit), the chat shows the error; it does not switch to another model.
- The Mac versions have not been tested on a real Mac yet.
- Help, screenshots and example prompts are in the [wiki](https://github.com/PockPock9/PockPockAgent/wiki).
